svg.title: B1.02 · Calculate Special Bonus
svg.desc: One row per employee with their calculated bonus. An odd ID gives 1. A permitted name also gives 1. Michael fails the name test and Juan fails the ID test. IDs 7 and 9 receive 7400 and 7700. The remaining employees receive 0 and all five appear in ID order. FROM Employees · one table is enough. Each employee row holds the ID and name that determine eligibility, plus the salary that determines the payout. Employees who receive zero still have an output row.
svg.text: One row per employee with their calculated bonus.
Michael has an odd ID. Does that alone earn a bonus?
A triangle marks an example to follow. A dark source band spans its columns. ƒ marks a calculated value. Deeper cell colors mark the values to
follow. SQL excerpts use … for omitted clauses.

g.aria-label: FROM Employees · one table is enough
g.text: FROM Employees · one table is enough
Each employee row holds the ID and name that determine eligibility, plus the salary that determines the payout.
Employees who receive zero still have an output row.

svg.text: An odd ID gives 1. A permitted name also gives 1. Michael fails the name test and Juan fails the ID test.
employee_id % 2 AS remainder, name NOT LIKE 'M%' AS name_allowed
IDs 7 and 9 receive 7400 and 7700. The remaining employees receive 0 and all five appear in ID order.
CASE WHEN name NOT LIKE 'M%' AND employee_id % 2 = 1 THEN salary ELSE 0 END
